# bob capture

Capture tasks, bullets, record notes, notebook notes, and Pomodoro commands into the vault

```text title="bob capture --help"
Capture one or more tasks, bullets, record notes, or notebook notes into the Bob Obsidian vault.

A route for an album `@dir/` or `@dir/^stem` creates a Record Note in that folder instead of a task. First-level `key:: value` bullets set schema fields; other first-level bullets become notes. `@dir/stem` updates an existing record: parent text is the first note, only supplied fields change, and the write keeps unrelated bytes. Dry-run and commit share the planned Markdown. A local record route wins over a draft-wide `@@route`. Incomplete or invalid records refuse the whole draft before any writes. Record types come from album schemas; they are not Task Types (`#fix`). See docs/records.md and docs/capture.md (Record notes).

A notebook destination writes a note instead of a task (`@nb`, `@nb#section`, `@nb^id`, `@nb+id`); `@@nb` is draft-wide. A complete `@parent^id@` caret seal plus `%n` creates a notebook. See docs/notebooks.md.

TEXT is split into ordered capture items by one or more blank or whitespace-only physical lines; leading, trailing, and repeated separators are ignored. A whitespace-separated line of only Pomodoro session operators is also split into one item per operator, so `+2 x` means `+2`, blank line, `x`. A '@@<route>' declaration token anywhere in the draft is metadata, not a capture item: every otherwise-unrouted item inherits that destination, while an item-local @route, @route+id, @route#..., @route^..., or @route:... marker still wins for that item. A `%n` item ignores the declaration and files a Pomodoro note, except a complete `@parent^id@` caret seal plus `%n`, which creates a notebook. A declaration-only draft fails. Do not combine a textual @@ declaration with --route, --section, --task, or --drawer. Each item's first nonblank line is normalized and becomes that item's parent, formatted as a #task with a [created::] stamp unless a bullet or sub-bullet route is selected, and written to mac_inbox.md unless an @route token, @@ declaration, or --route target is provided. Existing target files prefer a Tasks section, then fall back to the last top-level task block. Missing target files are created when needed.

Within each item, every later physical line must be either a column-zero Markdown bullet or a nested bullet prefixed by exactly two ASCII spaces. At either depth, '-', '*', or '+' must be followed by a space or tab; the source marker and separator are stripped and the item is rendered with the canonical '- <body>' marker. Column-zero authored items render one target-selected indentation unit beneath the parent; two-space source items render two units beneath the parent and attach to the nearest preceding nonempty column-zero authored item. A marker-only placeholder is skipped and never clears that owner. Unsupported indentation, prose continuation, or an orphaned nested item fails with a usage error naming the physical line, and so does an item left with no text once its own capture markers are removed. Every recognized terminal 's:<N>', '$<N>', '%...', and '@route' marker configures only its own capture item and is stripped from the rendered line it was typed on; a second line in the same item resolving the same marker is ambiguous and fails before anything is written. Only an item's first line keeps the established leading '@route text' form. Authored children render before any clipboard children and the priority schedule log.

Gmail URLs stay tasks. Saved threads link offline; other resolvable URLs are linked by a detached worker after capture. Capture never calls Gmail.

All items are planned against in-memory note snapshots before commit. Later items see earlier planned edits to the same target, and any parse, clipboard, validation, staging, or replace failure leaves notes, ledgers, and newly created clipboard files at their original state. Single-item JSON keeps its legacy shape; multi-item JSON keeps the first result at the top level and adds an ordered 'captures' array.

A maximal adjacent run of two or more @route+id targets at one end of a parent line applies that line to every named task in marker order, in the same atomic capture. Duplicate task identities are refused before staging. A target run shares each clipboard read and each rolled priority date; errors name the failing target. Human output shows a 'targets  @route+id · @route+id' header, and JSON adds per-member fanout context.

Move or merge whole tasks with `@a+x @b+y > @dest`, quoting the draft so the shell keeps the `>` (for example `bob capture '@inbox+bench > @db+upgrade'`). One or more `@route+id` sources precede a standalone `>` and one destination follows it: a bare `@route` moves the tasks into that note keeping their IDs, `@route+id` merges them into that task, `@route+id#drawer` merges into its drawer (an H2 section on `^prj`), and `@route#section` merges into that note section. The line carries nothing else: no body text, child bullets, schedule, priority, type, clipboard, dependency, relation, or completion markers. A glued arrow, extra text, children, or any other destination shape fails with a teaching error before anything is written. Later items see the staged move or merge, dry-run plans identically, and any failure rolls the whole batch back. Human output prints `↪ Moved N tasks into <note> › Tasks` for moves and `⤵ merged N tasks into “<target>”` for merges; JSON adds `moves[]` or `merges[]` plus `repaired_files[]`. When stdout is a regular file whose name starts with `@`, capture refuses with `shell_ate_transfer_arrow`: the shell ate an unquoted `>`. When draft arguments are present and stdin is a regular file whose name starts with `@`, capture refuses with `shell_ate_merge_in_arrow`: the shell ate an unquoted `<`.

A draft whose first item carries the `%t` directive expands one capture per later row. Write one capture item with `{0}`, `{1}`, and so on, put `%t` at either edge of any of its lines, then a blank line and one row of values per capture; each row must supply exactly one value per placeholder index; quote fields containing spaces. A template that uses only `{0}` takes one capture per value, so `bar baz bam` on one line is three captures. Capturing a template is exactly capturing its expansion, and the whole run still plans and writes atomically. Use `{{` and `}}` for literal braces, or the `--expand` option to print the expanded text without capturing. Templates refuse `%c` and Pomodoro session operators because those actions cannot safely repeat across rows.

Append a trailing lowercase 's:<N>' token, where N is a non-negative integer, to schedule the capture N days from today. The token is removed from the task text and rendered as [scheduled::YYYY-MM-DD] after [created::YYYY-MM-DD]. It may appear before or after a trailing @route token and is recognized only at the very end of the input. Checkbox-bearing captures with a resolved scheduled property start Blocked as '[?]', including s:0; ordinary bullet and sub-bullet forms stay checkbox-free.

Append a trailing '$' or '$<N>' token, where N selects the Nth priority level configured in ~/.config/bob/config.yml (1-4 today: P1-P4), to write [priority::<value>] and roll a random [scheduled::YYYY-MM-DD] inside that level's day window. A bare '$' means '$1'. A task with no priority field is implicitly P0, so there is no $0. An explicit s:<N> wins the scheduled date and $<N> still writes the priority. Like s:<N> it is recognized only in the terminal token region and may appear on either side of a trailing @route token. Single-quote '$<N>' in a shell; an unquoted or double-quoted $2 is expanded by the shell.

Append a lowercase '#<type>' token at either edge of any line to type the new task (#fix, #"DEEP WORK") or retype the existing task an item targets (whole-item links, Ensure Next, explicit toggle, relationship owners). A first-level bullet start (`- #requirements`) names a drawer instead; nest notes beneath it. A free-standing bare '#' at an item edge is incomplete: add a type (`#fix`) or write '\#' to keep a literal '#'. '#' plus a digit, '##…', '#-…', mid-line '#', and glued hashes stay ordinary prose. One marker per item; unknown names are refused with a suggestion. With a named Pomodoro, the marker must agree with its type or capture refuses. Retyping stages the field before the gesture and relocates the live Task Link to agree.

Append a `%` directive at either edge of any physical line, with only other markers between it and that edge. `%c` reads the clipboard into child bullets of this item; `%c<N>` (N ≥ 2) captures that many values, starting with the live clipboard and then recent history newest first. '%c1' is equivalent to '%c'; N is a count, not a history index. Counted history is used only when its newest entry matches the live clipboard within a 1.5-second wait, and otherwise the capture refuses. `%n` files the item as a Pomodoro note (see below) and composes with `%c`. `%l` queues a bare-URL reference with companion audio (see below); anywhere else it refuses. Each directive appears at most once per item. `%c` composes with s:<N>, $<N>, #<type>, and every route kind. On a note-less `@route+id` (or `@route+id#drawer`), `%c` files the clipboard lines as notes directly under that task (or drawer). Each clipboard value is classified separately: small text stays inline; 2-10 flat text lines and 1-10 flat unordered Markdown list items become child bullets, with source list markers removed; copied file paths are saved under img/ or file/; and long or other Markdown-structured text is preserved in a timestamped file/clip-*.md snippet. Clipboard children use the target note's dominant tab-or-two-space indentation and fall back to a tab. History captures fail without writing unless the exact requested count succeeds. A bare '%' is incomplete. Mid-line tokens such as '50%' stay prose. Use --clip to force a clipboard read as if '%c' were written. Use --no-clip to never read the clipboard, even when '%c' is written: a dry run reports clip.status not_read, and a real capture refuses. Clipboard failures abort before the note or attachment files are changed.

Use '@<route>:<block-id>' in the same leading or trailing position to create a next-status task and link it from today's Pomodoro ledger. The routed task renders as '- [*] #task <body> [created::YYYY-MM-DD] ^<block-id>' when unscheduled, or '[?]' with any scheduled property before the final block ID. An optional '#<pomodoro>' slug, as in '@<route>:<block-id>#<pomodoro>', first targets a named open Pomodoro instead of the implicit current-or-future choice; whole-slug matches beat earlier prefix matches, and a typed '#' with an empty name is incomplete. If no open name matches, capture creates a canonical named future entry as '- [ ] () — NAME' and puts the task link beneath it. The daily note comes from BOB_DAY_FILE or <bob-dir>/YYYY/YYYYMMDD.md. A bare capture places the link by the new task's type (running exact entry, else first open exact entry, else first open entry containing the type, else a created `— T` placeholder); with no effective type it prefers the single open timed entry in its Pomodoros section and otherwise uses the first open entry. Named creation inserts after the current Pomodoro's complete block, else after the last completed Pomodoro's complete block, else before the first Pomodoro. Existing named matches skip the multiple-open-timed guard; named creation uses that guard because it needs an unambiguous current anchor. Both notes are fully validated before either is replaced; duplicate block IDs, duplicate Pomodoro links, missing ledger structure, no eligible unnamed target, invalid Pomodoro names, and multiple open timed entries for implicit or named creation fail without a partial capture. Append '=<X>[#<pomodoro>]' to start the session atomically, as in '@<route>:<block-id>=3' or '@<route>:<block-id>=-2#deep-work': '<X>' mirrors the 'se<X>' snippet (empty, digits, '-', '-digits', or 'digits-' with optional digits; empty duration means 25 minutes, bare '-' means 5-minute offset, no '-' means zero offset). The start replaces the selected untimed '()' placeholder with '(**HHMM-HHMM** [t:: Nm])' computed from BOB_NOW at 5-minute rounding, then links the new task beneath it; any open timed entry fails with 'finish the current Pomodoro first'. The started entry moves ahead of every open Pomodoro, right after the last completed one. For '=', the first open placeholder wins, else an unnamed entry is created; for '#name=', an open name match wins, else a canonical named entry is created. '=<X>' cannot combine with 's:<N>' or '$<N>'.

Capture a whole item '@<route>:<block-id>[=<X>[#<pomodoro>]]' to link an existing task into today's Pomodoro ledger instead of creating one, as in `bob capture '@sase:deep-fix'` or `bob capture '@sase:deep-fix=bugs3'`. The marker must be the entire item: no body text, authored children, '%c', 's:<N>', '$<N>', or forced destination flags. Ready and Blocked tasks become Next (a valid future schedule is retired with a pull-forward log entry); Next and In Progress tasks keep their status. With '#<pomodoro>' the link moves to that named entry (creating it when needed); without a name an already-queued task stays in its Pomodoro and '=<X>' starts that entry and moves it to the front of the queue, otherwise the task's type places the started entry (the first untimed open entry it picks, or a created started `— T` entry). The '^' spelling ('bob capture '^sase:deep-fix='') executes identically and exists so typing '^' completes In Progress and Next tasks. JSON reports a distinct 'pomodoro_link' kind with the status transition, the ledger action (linked, moved, or already_current), and the resolved destination.

Capture a whole item `@<route>` with no section, task text, bullets, or other markers to inspect eligible Pending, Next, and Ready tasks in the root `<route>.md` note. The preview reads today's Pomodoros and shows each row's destination; it never selects or writes a row automatically. Choose offers with `-p 1,3`, `-p all`, or `-p none`: `bob capture @sase` previews the offers, and `bob capture -p 1,3 -- @sase` links offers 1 and 3.

A single-token, single-line item starting with ':' (for example ':' or ':dee') is a task-picker query, never a capture: it fails with a teaching error so an unfinished query cannot create a junk inbox task. Accepting the picked task in a picker inserts its '@<route>:<block-id>' link, which captures exactly like a typed link.

Capture a whole item `!note:block-id` (for example `!sase:fix-flaky`) to complete that existing open task without closing a Pomodoro, the way `x!N` completes a linked task: the task line closes exactly as `x!N` writes it (including embedded subtasks), its Task Links retire the way `bob task reconcile` retires them, and Blocked dependents recover the way Ctrl+Enter recovers them. A fully unblocked dependent is offered; a successor Task Link is created only for a `--pull-in` pick (docs/task-dependencies.md §12; `plan.link_unblocked: false` turns linking off). The token must be the entire item: no body text, children, `%`, `s:`, `$`, `#name`, `=`, `@@`, or forced destination flags. The note locator works vault-wide exactly like `&note:block-id` (`!projects/foo:bar`, `!"Shopping List":milk`). A bare `!` or partial token fails with a teaching error so an unfinished query cannot create a junk inbox task; accepting the picked task inserts its `!<note>:<block-id>` token. JSON reports kind `task_complete` with an additive `task_complete` object. Single-quote the argument: zsh history-expands `!`.

Append `&note:block-id` to make the captured task depend on an existing task (`&foo:bar`; quote notes with spaces: `&"Shopping List":milk`). Task text creates a new owner. An existing-task marker with no text (`@note+id`, bare `@note:id`, or bare `^note:id`) names that task as the owner and writes only the relationship. A `+` or `+query` token beside `&`/`*` opens the vault picker to choose the owner; submit refuses until a task is selected. Combine with `*note:block-id` in either order: `&` prerequisites of the owner land first.

Append `*note:block-id` to make the captured task a prerequisite of an existing open task (`*job:cleanup`; quote notes with spaces: `*"Shopping List":milk`). The named task gains a managed `DEPENDS ON` link to the captured task, flips to Blocked, and loses today's live Task Links; a new captured task is capped at Next. An existing owner selected with `@note+id`, bare `^note:id`, or `--task`/`--route` may rise as far as In Progress. A Done or Canceled owner cannot block; reopen it first. Combine with `&note:block-id` in either order: `&` prerequisites of the captured task land first.

Capture a whole item `+N` or `-N` (for example `+5` or `-2`) to adjust today's current timed Pomodoro by N five-minute units: `+5` extends by 25 minutes, `-2` shortens by 10 minutes. The count is optional and defaults to 1, so `+`, `-`, `++`, and `--` all work. The item must contain only the signed count (leading/trailing whitespace is fine); any extra text, marker, or child line fails instead of creating a task, and `Plan +5` stays ordinary prose. `+0`/`-0` fail, and oversized magnitudes fail checked arithmetic before any write. The adjustment selects the single open timed entry in today's `## Pomodoros` section, keeps the start fixed, recomputes `new_end = (start + new_duration) modulo 24 hours` with `new_duration = max(0, old + signed_units*5)`, and rewrites only that ledger line with its clock key: worked rows use `[t:: Nm]`, off-clock rows use `[off:: Nm]`, bare historical rows gain `[off:: Nm]`, and a conflict keeps `[t:: Nm]`, preserving other metadata, child bullets, and newline style. A `@@` declaration still routes ordinary items in the same draft but never turns an adjustment into a task. Forced destination, task, section, and clipboard options (`--route`, `--section`, `--task`, `--drawer`, `--clip`, `%`, `s:<N>`, `$<N>`) are rejected on adjustment items. Later items observe earlier staged edits to the same daily file, dry-run reports without writing, and any failure rolls the whole batch back. JSON reports a distinct `pomodoro_adjust` kind with an additive `pomodoro_adjust` object (direction, requested units/minutes, actual delta, before/after timing, line/name, rendered range); human output names what changed and where, and dry-run says what would change.

Capture a whole item `++N` or `--N` (for example `++3` or `--2`) to shift today's running timed Pomodoro N five-minute units later or earlier, keeping its duration: both endpoints translate modulo 24 hours like Obsidian's `N\o` / `N\O`. The count defaults to 1 (`++` / `--` move one unit); `++0` / `--0` and oversized magnitudes fail before any write, and the item must contain only the operator. JSON reports a distinct `pomodoro_shift` kind with an additive `pomodoro_shift` object; human output names what shifted and where, and dry-run says what would shift. The shell sees a leading `-` as a flag, so spell an earlier shift as `bob capture -- --2` (or `bob capture --1` for one unit); a bare `--` stays the end-of-options marker and carries no text.

Pomodoro sessions form a lifecycle: `=`/`=<X>` starts the next session, `=name` starts that named session, `+[N]`/`-[N]` resizes the running session, `++[N]`/`--[N]` shifts it, and `x` stops the running one. Mnemonic: `=` starts now, `x` stops now, `Nx` stops at N blocks, and `x=` records what already happened. Before `x`: 5-minute blocks · after `x`: task numbers. A whole-item `x=` token records past work (`x=3`, `x=build`, `x=build2 x=fix3`) ending at the next five-minute boundary; stack members fill earlier windows backward. It never changes a running session, and `!` only permits trimming one edge of a closed row. Session operators may share one line when whitespace separates them: `+2 x` means `+2`, blank line, `x`, and `x =` closes then starts the next session. Quote `=` items in zsh, which expands a leading `=word` to a command path.

Batches that change today's `## Pomodoros` section also report the plan budget: a top-level `plan_budget` object with the before/after link meter, an `added_themes` list of new type names, and a link-cap warning that fires only while the batch grows the meter past its cap. Human output prints one `plan L/Lc links` meter line after the result plus one `bob capture: warning: …` stderr line per fired warning, and names where each new Task Link landed (`→ into running GOALS (0945-1015)`, `→ under GOALS (next up)`, `→ under GOALS (named)`, or `→ new Pomodoro BOB`; JSON reports the same destination with a `role` of `current`, `next_up`, `named`, or `created`, plus a `type` object when Bob placed the link by the task's type). New types never warn and never refuse. An invalid plan config skips the budget with one plain warning. See `docs/capture.md` (`Plan budget`) and `docs/plan.md`.

Capture a whole item `=`/`=<X>` (for example `=`, `=3`, `=-2`, `=2-1`) to start today's next future Pomodoro now with the same timing as the `se<X>` snippet: empty is 25 minutes, `3` is 15 minutes, `-` is 25 minutes with a 5-minute offset, `2-1` is 10 minutes with a 5-minute offset. While an open MEET's event run occupies the start block, an unnamed start takes that MEET instead (an empty suffix writes the run's span). A named start uses a bare name directly after `=`: `=bugs`, `=3bugs`, `=bugs3`, `=fix3~2`. Bare names start with a letter, contain no `-`, do not end in a digit, and cannot read like a close. Use `#` only for a name that needs it, such as `=3#deep-work`, `=#2fa`, or `=#x2`; quoted names keep their quotes. `#` is needed when a bare spelling cannot express the name; Bob teaches the escaped selector when a bare name contains a dash. A timing can precede or follow a bare name (`=3bugs` or `=bugs3`); the old `@` separator and a second timing are retired and get a glued rewrite. `=bugs3~2` starts BUGS without queued Task Link 2. An open match (whole slug, else prefix) starts in place, a completed match starts a new session with that name (an again start), and otherwise a new named session is created and started. A trailing `~<K>` drop list (for example `=~2`, `=3~2,4`, `=bugs~2`, `=3bugs~1,3`) starts without those queued Task Links: `~` drops, so `=~2` drops task 2 from the session you start the way `x~2` drops task 2 from the session you stop, using the numbers the start lineup shows. The drop list comes last, after a name or timing. The item must contain only the start token (leading/trailing whitespace is fine) and have exactly one physical line; a claimed token (counted or drop-carrying) with extra text, markers, or child lines (`=3 more`, `=3x`, `=~2 more`) and an exact token with child lines fail instead of creating a task, while a bare token with prose (`= foo`, `= ~2`) and mid-body tokens (`Plan =3`, `Plan =bugs`) stay ordinary prose. A dangling `~`/`,` (`=~`, `=~2,`) is incomplete and fails. A bare `=`/`=<X>` start needs a future `- [ ] ()` placeholder; a named start creates its session when no open entry matches. With one timed entry running, `=` restarts it and `=<X>` restarts it with that timing. `=name` swaps a different named Pomodoro in and keeps the running clock; `=3name` swaps it in with fresh timing. Naming the running session with no timing refuses and teaches `=` or `=<X>` to restart it. The started entry moves to the current slot and reports its queued Task Links, numbered 1..N in ledger order with a numbered human index column. A `@@` declaration never applies to start items, and forced destination/task/section/clipboard options are rejected on them. Later items see earlier staged edits, dry-run reports without writing, and any failure rolls the whole batch back, so `x`, blank line, `=` switches sessions atomically.

The retired `==` start family fails with one teaching error that names its single-`=` rewrite: for example, `==3#deep-work` says to write `=3#deep-work`. The `==x` family is not a close and teaches the bare `x` rewrite. A bare `==` followed by prose stays ordinary text, preserving Obsidian highlights. JSON stays `pomodoro_start`; `pomodoro_start.override` is present only for a restart or swap and its action is `restart` or `swap`. See `docs/capture.md` (`Overriding the running Pomodoro`).

Capture a whole item `[N]x[<N>][*<P>][!<M>][~<K>][@<N>]` (lowercase `x` only, with `*`, `!`, `~`, and `@` in any order; `<N>` may instead be typed last as `@<N>` (for example `x!1@2` means `x2!1`)) to close today's running timed Pomodoro the way Obsidian's Ctrl+Enter completion does, plus an auto-decrement that shortens an early-stopped session to the earliest five-minute step at or after now (plain `x` never extends a session; an overrun is reported — write `Nx` to close at a stated size). A bare `x` keeps today's behavior; `x<N>` keeps only the numbered Task Links in `<N>` in progress and defers the rest, `x*<P>` parks the links in `<P>` (normal In Progress work without carrying them forward), `x!<M>` completes the links in `<M>`, `x~<K>` drops the links in `<K>` (removed from the closed session, not carried and not started; a dropped task keeps its lane), and combined forms do each part at once. Any numbered list, including `!<M>` or `~<K>` alone, makes the close explicit: unlisted plain Task Links defer without being started and carry to the continuation. Unlisted Event Tasks keep their clock outcomes; authored markers and wildcards keep their meanings. Thus `x!2` completes 2 and defers other plain links, while `x~2` drops 2 and defers them. `x0!2`, `x0~2`, and `x0*2` behave like `x!2`, `x~2`, and `x*2`. Completing planned tasks also links what they unblocked into the closed session's continuation (docs/task-dependencies.md §12; `plan.link_unblocked: false` turns linking off). `<N>`, `<P>`, `<M>`, and `<K>` are comma-separated task numbers in ledger order starting at 1 (the numbers `bob capture` shows, in human output, in `--dry-run`, and as JSON `task_links`); a lone `0` means no task stays in progress, as in `x0`. Plain `x0` on a note-free session resets it to the first future placeholder (clearing the parenthesized ledger to `()` and keeping all children); the same `x0` on a session with a stand-alone note closes, deferring every numbered link. Explicit modifiers (`x0*2`, `x0!2`, `x0~2`, wildcards) always close. A present `*` or `!` group with no digits selects every numbered link left after explicit assignments (`x*` parks all, `x!` completes all, `x1*` keeps 1 in progress and parks the rest, `x*!2` parks the rest and completes 2). Explicit forms such as `x*1`/`x!1` select only task 1; an absent group stays absent and `~` never defaults. Two empty wildcard groups compete, so `x*!` and `x!*` need numbers on at least one group. Glue one or two digits before the `x` (`2x`, `2x!2`, `2x0`) to close at exactly that many five-minute blocks from the session start: `2x!2` records 10 minutes then completes task 2, and may lengthen the session to do it. The number before `x` is the number of blocks Bob records, or Bob tells you why not: a size that has not elapsed yet, a session that has not started, or a time range that does not parse refuses with a named fix (`pomodoro_close_size_not_elapsed`, `pomodoro_close_size_not_started`, `pomodoro_close_size_unparseable`) and writes nothing. `2x0` closes and defers every plain link, never a reset. A sized close comes first on its line, after any `+`/`-`/`++`/`--` moves: `x 2x faster` logs `2x faster`, while `--1 2x!2` and `2x =` still chain. `0x` needs at least 1 block, three or more digits (`100x`) stay reserved, `=2x` is not a start, `2x=3` mixes a size with a past record, and a capital `X` (`2X4 lumber`) stays prose. Human output reads `0900-0925 → 0900-0910 (10m · 2x, −15m)` with no overrun line, and JSON carries an additive `size` object; after a `+`/`-` adjust plus an unsized close at a whole-block size, human output adds a dim `tip: 2x!2 closes at 10m in one step` line. Log one entry on the close line: `x wired the lexer` logs to the first task the close works (task 1 for a plain `x`, the first eligible worked link with wildcard intent), and `x1,3 3 fixed the flaky test` logs to task 3. A leading number names the task, so only the entry's first token is an index (`x 1 3 bugs fixed` logs `3 bugs fixed` to task 1). Write the entry right after the close, then any session operators (`bob capture 'x wired the lexer'`, `bob capture 'x1,3 3 fixed the flaky test'`, `bob capture 'x wired the lexer ='`). For several entries or details, use child bullets below the close instead: `- [<n>] <text>` logs `<text>` in typed order, `- * <text>` logs the same entry to every worked task no other entry in this close logs to, and a two-space `  - <detail>` nests an undated detail under its entry in the task's Work Log. Bullets are numbered all or none except star bullets, which never fix the list's kind: either every non-star first-level bullet starts with its task number (`- 3 foo bar`), or none does and each unnumbered bullet logs in order to the close's worked tasks — one worked task takes them all, otherwise bullet `i` logs to worked task `i`, so `x3,4` plus `- foo bar` plus `- baz bam` writes exactly what `- 3 foo bar` plus `- 4 baz bam` writes, and `x` plus `- wired the lexer` plus `- * code review` logs the first to task 1 and the star to every other worked task. A leading number is always a task number, so to log text that starts with a number, number every bullet (`- 3 2 bugs fixed`); to log text that starts with `*`, write `- * * foo` or `- 1 * foo`. For explicitly numbered selections without wildcards, positions resolve lexically and `capture-parse` agrees with `bob capture`. With wildcard intent, numbered entries can target resolved worked links except explicit drops; unnumbered bullets wait for the staged top-level worked lineup, and an unnumbered inline entry logs once to its first eligible link. With a numbered list and no wildcard, only the explicit numbers in `<N>`, `*<P>`, or `!<M>` take entries; otherwise every number starting at 1 is lexically eligible except `~<K>`, with actual outcomes checked at execution. `x!2 note` logs to task 2; `x~2 note` fails because the selection works no task. Only the first token is an index, so `- 1 fixed 3 bugs` logs `fixed 3 bugs` and every backslash stays literal. The outcome is exactly the sub-bullets the user would type by hand under that Task Link, followed by the unchanged close. A close's child lines are Work Log bullets; a token ending in `,` or `~` (`x1,`, `x*1,`, `x*~`) is incomplete and fails, a dangling bullet (`- 1` or `- *`) or dangling inline number (`x 1`) is incomplete and fails, whitespace is never allowed inside the lists, and `xx`/`xa`/`Plan x`/a capitalized `X…` stay ordinary prose. A trailing `*`/`!` with no numbers is a valid wildcard group instead of a dangling state, so `x*` and `x!` are valid. Entry text is literal (`@route`, `@@route`, `s:<N>`, `$<N>`, `%`, `#`, and `:query` stay text; plain wikilinks are allowed), while block links, embeds, and code fences are rejected. An inline entry plus child bullets fails with the bullet to write. A chain line's bullets attach to its `x`, and an inline entry chains too (`x wired the lexer =` closes with the entry then starts, `-2 x wired the lexer` shortens then closes). `@route:block-id=x…` (and the `^` forms; the `=` separates the suffix from the block ID, and the retired `=*…`/`=!…` aliases fail with a teaching error) first put that existing task into the running session then close it, and `<text> @route:block-id=x…` creates the new task in the running session then closes it; explicit numbers and wildcard expansion refer to the post-link lineup, and `#name` with a close fails because only the running session can close. Later items see earlier staged edits, dry-run reports without writing, and any failure rolls the whole batch back, so `printf -- '-2\n\nx\n' | bob capture` adjusts then closes atomically. JSON reports a distinct `pomodoro_close` kind (link and task forms keep their kind with an additive `pomodoro_close` object) carrying the typed `raw`, the `in_progress`/`park`/`complete`/`drop` lists, the `log` entries (`index`, `text`, `details`, and an `all` flag on expanded star copies) in typed order, the numbered `task_links` lineup (with `parked` and `dropped` outcomes), each task row's `index` and `role` (with a `dropped` role; parked rows stay `worked` with `carried: false`) plus its `typed_work_log` subset and the aligned `typed_work_log_details`; human output names the session, the range change, the file, and the line, prefixing numbered rows with their index, printing typed entries first uncapped and not dimmed, listing dropped rows (with a `stays <status>` lane caption), marking parked rows `Parked · not carried`, and summarizing `Parked <P>` and `Dropped <K>`. Single-quote the argument: zsh expands a leading `=word` and `!` history expansion applies.

Use '@<route>^<block-id>' in the same leading or trailing position to create an ordinary open task with the requested trailing Obsidian block ID, without creating or modifying a Pomodoro ledger link. It renders as '- [ ] #task <body> [created::YYYY-MM-DD] ^<block-id>' when unscheduled, or '[?]' with priority and scheduled properties before the final block ID. Duplicate block IDs in the destination note fail before the note is replaced; a missing destination note may still be created like any ordinary routed task. This form never reads or requires the daily note. The retired '@<route>::<block-id>' spelling is no longer accepted; use '@<route>^<block-id>' instead.

Append '@' immediately after the block ID, as in '@<route>^<block-id>@' with an optional '#<pomodoro>' name ('@<route>^<block-id>@#<pomodoro>'), to create a brand-new sub-project note '<route>_<block-id with every '-' replaced by '_'>.md' at the vault root instead of a task. The note carries a 'parent: "[[<route>]]"' link, a '[[project]]' type with 'wip' status, and a '- [ ] #task #prj <body> #hide ^prj' lifecycle task, mirroring the Obsidian 'Create project note from task' command. The '^prj' task is never linked and never starts as '[*]'. The route is lower-cased and the block ID keeps its authored case. The parent '<route>.md' must already exist as an area or non-terminal project note; the new note must not exist yet. Moving a task removes its complete block from the parent and repairs links; the parent is replaced last, while 'bob projects sync' owns its Sub-projects line. Authored child bullets become '## Tasks' entries or '## Title Case' sections from ALL-CAPS titles in the new note. In that item's first-level bullets, '- ^<id>' moves an open top-level task from the parent into that slot; '- :<id>' also makes it Next and links it into the chosen Pomodoro. Moved blocks keep their children and identity. Write '- ^^' alone on its first-level line to choose several parent tasks after Return: answer with '-m/--move-in' (none, all, or row numbers/keys, a leading ':' also links, repeatable); picks land at the '^^' slot in parent order exactly as authored '- ^id' / '- :id' bullets, with ID-less picks gaining IDs in the batch. A dry run without '-m' previews rows as none; a real run without '-m' refuses. When there are no move bullets but the parent has movable tasks, the preview shows a '- ^' move hint. 's:<N>' writes inline '[scheduled:: YYYY-MM-DD]' on the '^prj' line and '$<N>' writes an inline priority there, while '%...' and --clip are rejected. The '#<pomodoro>' name picks the Pomodoro that ' :<id>' Task Links go under; with no such task the name is rejected as unused. The retired '@<route>^<block-id>+' and '@<route>:<block-id>+' spellings are no longer accepted; write '@<route>^<block-id>@' instead, or '@<route>:<block-id>@' to also choose which of the new note's tasks to link. End a first-level task bullet with ' :<block-id>' to name it, make it Next ('[*]', or '[?]' when the project is scheduled), and link '[[<stem>#^<block-id>]]' into the current/next Pomodoro or the named one; end it with ' ^<block-id>' to name it only. Named tasks render the ID last, after '[created::...]'. The project note and the daily note are written together, so a duplicate link or a missing daily note writes nothing. Seal with ':' instead of '^', as in '@<route>:<block-id>@' with an optional '#<pomodoro>' name, to create the same project note and then offer its open tasks (never '^prj', never the placeholder) as successor offers: each pick links exactly like an authored ' :<id>' bullet. Nothing is linked by default or with '-p none'; '-p <N>', '-p <key>', and '-p all' select offers, and the choice-required flow refuses the batch while offers exist and no pick was made. With no open task to offer or link, the '#<pomodoro>' name is rejected.

Use '@<route>+<block-id>' in the same leading or trailing position to capture an ordinary child bullet beneath an existing task without a [created::] stamp. It renders as '- <body>' and writes only the optional scheduled property. The complete new child is placed before the selected task's first direct-child Schedule Log or Work Log; if neither managed log exists, the child is appended at the end of the task block. The note and task must already exist. Existing child indentation and line endings are preserved; run 'bob capture-tasks -r <route>' to list eligible task block IDs. A trailing '#<drawer>' component, as in '@<route>+<block-id>#<drawer>', names an ALL-CAPS child drawer of that task. The selector is a slug or quoted literal; matching is exact by key, with reserved and near-duplicate refusals, and a missing drawer is created. The captured block is appended at the end of that drawer, before a managed log nested under it, using the drawer's child indentation. On the project note's own '^prj' task the selector instead names one of the note's eligible '##' sections, appending the block after that section's last nonblank line and creating a new '## Title Case' section at the end of the note when missing. '@<route>+<block-id>#' with an empty selector is incomplete and needs a drawer; run 'bob capture-drawers -r <route> -i <block-id>' to list them. A marker-only '@<route>+<block-id>' item with no body text ensures that task is Next and relocates its existing open-Pomodoro Task Link to the Pomodoro the task's type places without creating a missing link or toggling Next back to Ready. A separate '#<type>' after the marker, as in '@<route>+<block-id> #<type>', also retypes the existing task before ensuring Next and choosing the destination from its new type. With body text, '@<route>+<block-id>#<drawer>' keeps its drawer meaning, and a separate '#<type>' retypes the target in the same transaction. Neither unsuffixed form synthesizes a missing Task Link. A terminal '!' on the unsuffixed marker-only form, '@<route>+<block-id>!', is the only spelling that toggles the Pomodoro Task Link itself: when no matching link sits under an open Pomodoro the task links (Ready/Blocked rise to Next while Next/In Progress keep their lane), and when a matching link is already there every such link is removed with the lane unchanged. To retype during an explicit toggle, put '#<type>' after the bang, as in '@<route>+<block-id>! #<type>'; '@<route>+<block-id>#<type>!' is refused. A note-less '@<route>+<block-id>' (or '@<route>+<block-id>#<drawer>') item files each first-level bullet as its own note: plain bullets become notes under the task, drawer bullets (a leading '#slug' or an ALL-CAPS title with nested notes) file into that task's drawers, and '@<route>+<block-id>#<drawer>' with no note text files every bullet inside that drawer. Item-wide 's:<N>', '$<N>', '%c', and --clip are refused on this form, while a separate '#<type>' retypes the target and '&', '*', '~' keep it as owner.

Append `%n` at either edge of any physical line to capture the item as a plain-text sub-bullet on a Pomodoro instead of a task, or to create a notebook on a complete `@parent^id@` caret seal. A Pomodoro note renders as '- <body>' with no [created::] stamp, no '#task' marker, and no block ID. The daily note comes from BOB_DAY_FILE or <bob-dir>/YYYY/YYYYMMDD.md. Capture prefers the single open timed entry in its Pomodoros section, otherwise the last completed entry, and otherwise the first open entry, appending the new bullet at the end of that entry's child block. The marker composes with '%c' and --clip but is rejected alongside 's:<N>', '$<N>', '#<type>', and --route; a complete '@parent^id@' caret seal plus '%n' creates a notebook, and every other '@route' form is rejected. A draft-wide '@@route' does not apply to a `%n` item. Append `%l` at either edge of a bare-URL item to queue the reference with companion audio; anywhere else `%l` refuses.

Append '#<section-prefix>' or a bare '#' to an @route token (such as '@notes#Ideas' or '@notes#') to capture an ordinary bullet instead. It renders as '- <body> [created::YYYY-MM-DD]' and is placed in a non-Tasks section whose heading title starts with the prefix (compared case insensitively), or any non-Tasks section for a bare '#'. The Next & In Progress, Blocked, and Done & Canceled status-group headings bob task reconcile generates under a Tasks heading belong to that Tasks section and are never bullet targets. A matching non-H1 section is preferred; a matching H1 heading is used only when no non-H1 heading matches. The marker may lead ('@notes#Ideas jot idea') or trail ('jot idea @notes#Ideas') the body. A standalone terminal '#<section-prefix>' marker (not appended to an @route token) is still not accepted and fails with a usage error.

Use --route with --section to force bullet mode while keeping @tokens literal. The section title is matched exactly, case insensitively, against non-Tasks headings (generated status-group headings under Tasks are skipped); if no heading matches, the bullet falls back to the pre-heading section.

Use --route with --task and --drawer TITLE to nest a sub-bullet under the named ALL-CAPS child drawer of that task. The title is matched exactly, case insensitively; unlike a typed #<drawer> selector, it is not slug- or prefix-matched, so --drawer future-work does not match FUTURE WORK. On a '^prj' parent it matches the project note's eligible '##' sections instead, creating a missing section in Title Case.

Use expansion mode to print a template draft's expanded capture text and exit before vault access or planning. In expansion mode all other capture options are accepted and ignored.

Usage: bob capture [OPTIONS] [TEXT]...

Arguments:
  [TEXT]...
          Task text; multiple args are joined with spaces; an unknown `--flag` where TEXT would begin is rejected, later tokens stay literal

Options:
  -b, --bob-dir <DIR>
          Bob vault root; defaults to BOB_DIR or ~/bob

  -X, --cancel-offer <N|KEY[=REASON]>
          Cancel one offer; REASON goes to its Cancel Log. Repeatable, one offer per flag

  -c, --clip
          Force a clipboard read as if %c were written

  -x, --complete-offer <PICKS>
          Mark offer(s) Done; PICKS is a comma list. Repeatable

  -D, --drawer <TITLE>
          Nest under the exact drawer TITLE; requires --route and --task

  -d, --dry-run
          Plan and report without writing notes or clipboard files

  -E, --expand
          Print the draft with its `%t` template expanded, then exit without capturing

  -f, --format <FORMAT>
          Output format: human or json

          [default: human]
          [possible values: human, json]

  -h, --help
          Show help

  -i, --inbox-route <ANSWER>
          Route an inbox task this capture changes: <N|KEY>=<NOTE> moves it, <N|KEY>= keeps it in its inbox, keep keeps every otherwise unanswered candidate; repeatable

  -m, --move-in <PICKS>
          Answer a - ^^ move choice: none, all, or a comma list of row numbers and keys; a leading : also links; repeatable

  -n, --no-clip
          Never read the clipboard, even when %c is written

  -R, --no-ref
          Keep bare links as inbox tasks instead of queueing them for the reading queue

  -p, --pull-in <PICKS>
          Pull in successor offers: all, none, or a comma list of offer numbers and keys ($<N> in TEXT is still priority)

  -r, --route <NAME>
          Force the route to NAME.md and keep @tokens in text literal

  -s, --section <TITLE>
          Force a bullet into the exact section TITLE; requires --route

  -t, --task <BLOCK-ID>
          Append beneath task BLOCK-ID; requires --route

Examples:
  bob capture buy milk @groceries
  bob capture buy milk s:1
  bob capture buy milk s:2 @groceries
  bob capture buy milk @groceries s:2
  bob capture buy milk '$2'
  bob capture research rust '$4' @dev
  bob capture buy milk %c
  bob capture research links %c3
  bob capture investigate %c @dev:blockid
  bob capture --clip -- save dashboard
  bob capture '@dev^foobar' 'Some ordinary task.'
  bob capture '@dev:foobar' 'Some foobar task.'
  bob capture '@dev:foobar#bugs' 'Some foobar task.'
  bob capture '@cash^goog-exit@' 'Finish the Google exit packet!'
  bob capture @sase
  bob capture -p 1,3 -- @sase
  printf 'Finish the Google exit packet! @cash^goog-exit@\n- Draft the resignation memo\n' | bob capture
  printf 'Finish the Google exit packet! @cash^goog-exit+#admin\n- Draft the resignation memo :draft-memo\n  - keep it short\n- Collect the equity paperwork ^equity-docs\n' | bob capture
  printf 'Finish the Google exit packet! @cash:goog-exit@\n- Draft the resignation memo\n- Collect paperwork\n' | bob capture
  bob capture -p all -- '@cash:goog-exit@' 'Finish the Google exit packet!'
  printf 'Finish the Google exit packet! @cash^goog-exit@\n- ^^\n' | bob capture -m 1,:2
  bob capture '@cash+goog-exit' 'Called Morgan Stanley today.'
  bob capture '@cash+goog-exit!'
  bob capture +5
  bob capture -- -2
  bob capture +
  bob capture ++3
  bob capture -- --2
  bob capture --1
  bob capture -- --anything
  printf '+5\n\nCall bank @Cash+\n' | bob capture
  printf -- '--2\n\n+\n' | bob capture
  bob capture 'x'
  bob capture 'x2'
  bob capture 'x1!2'
  bob capture 'x!1@2'
  bob capture 'x1~2'
  bob capture 'x0'
  printf 'x2,3\n- 2 wired the lexer\n' | bob capture
  printf 'x =\n- 1 wired the lexer\n' | bob capture
  bob capture '='
  bob capture '=3'
  bob capture '=~2'
  bob capture '=3bugs~1'
  bob capture '=bugs'
  bob capture '=3bugs'
  bob capture '=bugs3'
  bob capture 'x =bugs'
  bob capture '@sase:deep-fix=bugs'
  bob capture 'x =~2'
  printf 'x\n\n=\n' | bob capture
  bob capture '+2 x'
  bob capture 'x ='
  bob capture '^bob:capture-stop=x'
  bob capture '^bob:capture-stop=x!1'
  bob capture -p 1 -- '!sase:fix'
  bob capture -p all -- '!sase:fix'
  bob capture -i 1=health -- '@mac_inbox:route-task'
  printf -- '-2\n\nx\n' | bob capture
  bob capture 'Postgres 17 minimum @foo+bar#requirements'
  bob capture --route foo --task bar --drawer REQUIREMENTS -- 'Postgres 17 minimum'
  bob capture remembered to bump the timeout %n
  bob capture paste the failing output %c %n
  bob capture jot idea @notes#Ideas
  bob capture --route notes --section Ideas -- jot idea
  bob capture @notes#Ideas jot idea
  printf '@@foo\nFirst task\n\nSecond task @bar\n' | bob capture
  printf 'Apply to {0}! @job^apply-{1} %%t\n\nFoobar foo\n"Two Sigma" two-sigma\n' | bob capture
  echo 'buy milk @groceries' | bob capture
  bob capture -f json -- @work send status
  printf 'Prepare launch\n- Confirm owner\n\nSend status @work\n' | bob capture
  printf 'Prepare launch\n- Confirm owner\n- Attach checklist\n' | bob capture
  bob capture https://example.com/essay
  printf 'Ramen Nagi @eat/\n- status:: liked\n- category:: Ramen\n' | bob capture
  bob capture 'Ask Kelly *job:cleanup'
  bob capture '*job:cleanup @body+work'
  bob capture '&foo:bar @body+excercise'
  bob capture '^body:excercise &foo:bar'
  bob capture '@inbox+bench @work+pgdump > @db'
  bob capture '@inbox+bench @work+pgdump > @db+upgrade'
  bob capture '@inbox+bench > @db+upgrade#future-work'
  bob capture '@mac_inbox+ws-proto > @dev#future-work'

Environment:
  BOB_CAPTURE_TEMPLATES_FILE  exact saved-template shelf path; defaults to $XDG_STATE_HOME/bob-cli/capture/templates.json
  BOB_CLIPBOARD_CMD          whitespace-split command that prints the live clipboard; overrides platform tools
  BOB_CLIPBOARD_HISTORY_CMD  whitespace-split history command; receives count and prints a newest-first JSON array of strings
  BOB_CONFIG_FILE            exact bullet-property config file; defaults to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/bob/config.yml or ~/.config/bob/config.yml
  BOB_DAY_FILE               exact daily note used by Pomodoro-linked capture
  BOB_DIR                    Bob vault root when --bob-dir is omitted
  BOB_GMAIL_KICK             off, 0, or false disables background Gmail linking
  BOB_NOW                    current date/time override
  BOB_PRIORITY_ROLL_SEED     fixed seed for $<N> rolls; unset means random
  XDG_CONFIG_HOME            base config directory for BOB_CONFIG_FILE's default; defaults to ~/.config
  XDG_STATE_HOME             base state directory for the saved-template shelf; defaults to ~/.local/state

Clipboard source order:
  Live: BOB_CLIPBOARD_CMD; macOS pbpaste; Linux wl-paste or xclip/xsel; tmux show-buffer
  History: BOB_CLIPBOARD_HISTORY_CMD; otherwise capture.clipboard_history (default auto: read-only Alfred, then Clipy, on macOS); no automatic provider elsewhere
```
